newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares knocked to close by new rand low.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares knocked to close by new rand low.

text.p: Battling to shrug off earlier comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals, South African shares were knocked by a nervous rand which slid to a new low against the dollar.
Suffering from softness for much of the week, shares lost ground soon after the rand hit a new all-time low against the dollar. It was last bid at 4.6110 against the U.S. currency.
Speaking at a conference in Johannesburg, Stals said that the central bank might need to tighten monetary policy if there was no slowdown in bank credit extension and money supply growth.
He said later that he saw no immediate need to increase interest rates at this stage.
Hoping for support from Wall Street in the wake of the falling rand, shares were disappointed by an initial soft start by U.S. shares and so closed weaker, dealers said.
Traders said foreigner investors were scarce and that trade was mostly in select quality stocks.
September M3 preliminary money supply data, due at 1500 GMT, was likely to offer more direction for Monday's trade. September trade data earlier had no impact on the equity market.
Gold shares lost strength as bullion clung to weaker levels below $383 an ounce.
The overall index was off 31.2 points to 6,985.2, industrials lost 15.1 points to 8,258.9 and golds were off 9.9 points to 1,703.8.
